title: Flatten page views
prompt: A reporting tool can't read nested columns. Write `solve(page_views)` so it returns every page view with each nested field pulled up into its own top-level column, keeping the field's own name.
rules: `type` and `os` come from `device`; `referrer` from `context`; `source` and `campaign` from `context.utm`.
A nested value that is missing at any level gives a missing value. Keep every page view.
hints: `page_views.printSchema()` shows which fields sit inside `device`, `context` and `context.utm`.
A dot path ending in `.*` expands every field of a struct into its own column.
One `select` can mix plain names, `.*` paths and single-field dot paths. Expanding all of `context` would bring the `utm` struct along as one column, so take `context`'s plain field on its own.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(page_views):
    # Every page view with its nested fields as top-level columns.
    return page_views
